paper_a.title: Asynchronous Methods for Deep Reinforcement Learning (Mnih et al., 2016)

paper_b.title: Simple Statistical Gradient-Following Algorithms for Connectionist Reinforcement Learning (Williams, 1992)

metadata.description: A3C extends Williams' REINFORCE policy gradient with three major additions: (1) a learned value function baseline (making it an actor-critic, with the advantage replacing raw returns), (2) n-step returns (replacing full Monte Carlo rollouts), and (3) asynchronous parallel actor-learners for decorrelation and speed. The core policy gradient principle -- updating parameters proportional to the score function times the return -- is inherited directly from REINFORCE.

matches.explanation: A3C explicitly cites and uses the REINFORCE policy gradient: $\nabla_\theta \log \pi(a_t | s_t; \theta)(R_t - b_t)$. This is the identical score-function estimator that Williams derived. A3C specializes the baseline $b_t$ to a learned value function $V(s_t; \theta_v)$.

Both use baseline subtraction for variance reduction. REINFORCE: generic baseline $b(s_t)$, optimal choice is approximately $V^\pi(s_t)$. A3C: explicitly learns $V(s_t; \theta_v)$ as a neural network sharing parameters with the policy, and uses the advantage $A_t = R_t - V(s_t; \theta_v)$ as the signal. A3C instantiates REINFORCE's theoretical suggestion with a practical learned critic.

A3C uses n-step returns $R_t = \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} \gamma^k r_{t+k} + \gamma^n V(s_{t+n})$ which bootstrap after $n$ steps using the value function. REINFORCE uses full Monte Carlo returns (no bootstrapping). The n-step truncation reduces variance at the cost of introducing bias from the value function estimate.

Asynchronous multi-threaded training with parallel actor-learners is entirely novel in A3C. REINFORCE is a single-threaded algorithm. The parallelism provides decorrelation (replacing experience replay) and linear speedup.
Entropy regularization ($H(\pi)$ bonus in the loss) to prevent premature convergence is an A3C addition not present in REINFORCE.
REINFORCE's proof that the score function estimator is unbiased for any baseline is the theoretical foundation that A3C inherits. A3C does not re-derive this result but relies on it.
REINFORCE's high variance problem motivates A3C's innovations: the learned baseline (advantage) and n-step returns both directly address variance reduction.

Both note the generality of policy gradient methods. REINFORCE: works with any differentiable stochastic policy. A3C: demonstrates this generality by succeeding on both discrete (Atari) and continuous (MuJoCo) action spaces with the same algorithm.
